hints: Rationalise $\dfrac{5z}{1+2i}$ and equate the real and imaginary parts of the equation separately to zero.
Use the linear equation from the imaginary part to express one variable in terms of the other.
Substitute into the real equation, solve the resulting quadratic, and pair each real coordinate with its corresponding imaginary coordinate.
walkthrough:
Let $z = x + \mathrm{i}y$, where $x$ and $y$ are real numbers. Then its complex conjugate is $z^* = x - \mathrm{i}y$, and:
$$zz^* = (x + \mathrm{i}y)(x - \mathrm{i}y) = x^2 + y^2$$

Simplify the fraction $\dfrac{5z}{1 + 2\mathrm{i}}$ by multiplying numerator and denominator by the complex conjugate $(1 - 2\mathrm{i})$:
$$\dfrac{5(x + \mathrm{i}y)(1 - 2\mathrm{i})}{(1 + 2\mathrm{i})(1 - 2\mathrm{i})} = \dfrac{5[(x + 2y) + \mathrm{i}(y - 2x)]}{1^2 - (2\mathrm{i})^2} = \dfrac{5[(x + 2y) + \mathrm{i}(y - 2x)]}{1 + 4} = (x + 2y) + \mathrm{i}(y - 2x)$$

Substitute this expression and $zz^* = x^2 + y^2$ into the given equation:
$$[(x + 2y) + \mathrm{i}(y - 2x)] - (x^2 + y^2) + 30 + 10\mathrm{i} = 0$$

Separate into real and imaginary parts:
$$\text{Real part: } x + 2y - (x^2 + y^2) + 30 = 0$$
$$\text{Imaginary part: } y - 2x + 10 = 0$$

Solve the linear imaginary equation for $y$ in terms of $x$:
$$y - 2x + 10 = 0 \implies y = 2x - 10$$

Divide the entire quadratic equation by $-5$:
$$x^2 - 9x + 18 = 0$$

Calculate the corresponding values of $y$ using $y = 2x - 10$:
$$\text{For } x = 3: \quad y = 2(3) - 10 = 6 - 10 = -4 \implies z = 3 - 4\mathrm{i}$$
$$\text{For } x = 6: \quad y = 2(6) - 10 = 12 - 10 = 2 \implies z = 6 + 2\mathrm{i}$$

State the final solutions in the form $x + \mathrm{i}y$:
$$z = 3 - 4\mathrm{i} \quad \text{and} \quad z = 6 + 2\mathrm{i}$$
